messages:
Priya (Support): FYI urgent customer escalation from acme-inc. They opened a ticket saying p99 latency jumped ~2x after yesterday's deploy (customer sees ~700ms p99 for /v1/generate) while our dashboard shows ~320ms. They provided a sample request-id: r-0a1b2c3d and said the difference persists across regions. Can oncall take a look?

Alex (oncall): Thanks Priya. Can you paste the exact request-id + any SDK details? Also pinging @Sam and @Lina since this smells like a metrics mismatch (rollup vs raw).

Priya (Support): request-id r-0a1b2c3d, sdk-js v2.4.1, customer is calling via server-side from EU region. They sent a screenshot of their client-side timing + the dashboard panel. They explicitly measured end-to-end ~700ms p99 using repeated curl calls.

Sam (sre): Quick sanity checks: 1) Are we comparing the same percentile definition? Grafana panels sometimes point at a rollup table that approximates quantiles. 2) Are they measuring client-side (including network + retry) vs server-side?

Priya (Support): They said they were measuring API response time from their backend (so should be server-side). No retries in their script.

Lina (metrics): Looking at the panel config for the public customer-latency board — it's using our aggregated rollup series (dataset=rollup_v2) and a 5m range vector. Rollups get pre-bucketed histograms with boundary normalization to a coarse set which can compress extreme tails. If a customer has many bursts, rollups will smooth p99 downward.

Alex (oncall): Can you show the promql/query that's powering that panel?

Lina (metrics): Panel uses this (simplified):
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(api_request_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
```
But the underlying stored series are the rollup buckets not the raw per-instance histograms. For single-tenant slices (customer label) we sometimes lose granularity due to bucket alignment and our ingest-time downsampling.

Mateo (platform): We changed histogram bucket normalization in the ingest pipeline last week to reduce cardinality. That change aligned bucket edges to a canonical set; it can introduce an off-by-one bucket boundary effect for customers whose latencies sit just above a boundary. Ops bot shows the change triggered at 2026-03-02T18:28:12Z.

ops-bot: config-change: metric_ingest.bucket_normalization=canonical-edges-v2 applied by deploy-bot at 2026-03-02T18:28:12Z

Sam (sre): That matches timeline. If their p99 sits near a bucket boundary, normalization can shift many values into the lower bucket during rollup, lowering the observed quantile. The customer's raw traces would still show the true p99.

Alex (oncall): Two immediate asks: 1) Priya, can you request a short raw trace/span dump for r-0a1b2c3d? 2) Lina, can you run the raw (non-rollup) query scoped to that customer and route?

Priya (Support): Got it. Asking customer for raw timing header and will share.

Lina (metrics): Ran a quick raw query (bypassing rollup) against the raw-series hotpath and got p99 ~680ms for that route with label customer=acme-inc over the same window. So the discrepancy is definitely the rollup.

Sam (sre): Confirmed. This is a metrics-aggregation artifact, not a runtime regression. We should explain to customer and provide mitigations.

Mateo (platform): Short-term mitigation options:
- Route their traffic to non-rollup metrics (enable high-cardinality telemetry for them for 24h).
- Temporarily disable bucket-normalization for the tenant (costly but doable).
- Update dashboard panel to use raw-series query for customer-scoped views.

Priya (Support): Customer asked for a fix asap. They want to know whether the backend actually regressed or if this is just our dashboard lying. How should I phrase this to them?

Alex (oncall): Say: "We investigated and found the difference is due to an aggregation change at ingest that reduces histogram resolution for rollups. Your raw request traces show the ~700ms p99; the public dashboard uses pre-aggregated rollups which underestimates tails. We're enabling higher-fidelity telemetry for your tenant and will follow up with a permanent fix." Keep it concise and apologetic.

Lina (metrics): I'll open an off-cycle job to pin the panel to raw-series for tenant-scoped views and run a comparison graph. Also creating an issue to evaluate bucket edges alignment for high-tail clients: ENG-9876.

Sam (sre): Also want to record repro steps so we can validate any future change. Priya, can you ask customer to run this script (should reproduce p99 quickly):
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDDO" -H "x-customer-id: acme-inc" \
    -H "x-request-id: r-$i" \
    -d '{"input":"'$(python -c 'print("X"*2000)')'"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate >/dev/null &\
  sleep 0.05\
done; wait
```
This will create bursts and should surface tail latency. Ask them to capture timings and the x-request-ids of slow responses.

Priya (Support): Sent script to customer, asked for 10 slow x-request-ids. Also offered to enable tenant telemetry for 24h.

Mateo (platform): I'll spin up a temporary telemetry override for acme-inc (no bucket normalization) for 24h. Watch for storage increase.

Lina (metrics): After enabling raw telemetry, we should correlate raw histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(...))) vs the rollup value and take snapshots. I'll post graphs here once we have the data.

Sam (sre): Next steps for permanent mitigation (post-mitigation):
- Revisit canonical bucket edges to reduce off-by-one tail effects.
- Add a dashboard note explaining rollup limitations for p95/p99.
- Add an automated alert when difference between raw and rollup p99 > 20% for a tenant.

Alex (oncall): Agreed. For now mark this as triaged. Priya, update the ticket with: we found the cause (ingest bucket normalization), we enabled a high-fidelity telemetry override, and we will follow up with ENG-9876. Mention expected 24h lookback.

Priya (Support): Done — updated ticket and customer notified with explanation + ETA. Customer asked if this explains billing differences (they saw more billed compute during spike). I told them that's separate — billing is computed on request units and retries, we'll investigate billing if they share traces.

Mateo (platform): ops-bot will post a storage-usage warning if telemetry override pushes > 20% storage.

ops-bot: alert: telemetry-override acme-inc storage_estimate=+28% threshold=20%

Lina (metrics): Posting initial comparison graphs now (links): https://grafana.redwood.local/d/cmp/acme-raw-vs-rollup (private link) :eyes:

Sam (sre): Thanks team. I'll draft a short blameless postmortem about the bucket-normalization change and its customer impact. Assigning follow-up tasks: ENG-9876 -> Lina, ENG-9877 (alerts) -> Sam.

Alex (oncall): Nice work. Priya, please keep customer updated hourly until we capture the 24h window.

Priya (Support): Will do. Closing the escalation for oncall; keeping ticket open for follow-up tasks. :white_check_mark:
